episodes.184560: Cold air funnels developed across central Ohio during the afternoon hours. One of these touched down, causing minor damage.
episodes.184664: Clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms developed over southwest Indiana, producing several reports of large hail. The storms developed near and south of a warm front that extended eastward across the lower Ohio Valley from weak low pressure over southwest Illinois. As surface temperatures cooled with the onset of nocturnal cooling, the storms became mostly elevated in nature. Aloft, a layer of more unstable air persisted due to moist south-southeasterly flow. Most-unstable layer capes (1000 to 850 mb) remained near 1000 j/kg. The primary severe weather hazard with these elevated storms was large hail. Effective bulk wind shear values near 30 to 35 knots were marginally favorable for organized convection.
episodes.184667: A cluster of severe thunderstorms formed over northwest Kentucky and the Pennyrile region during the late evening hours. These storms produced numerous reports of large hail and a couple of marginally severe wind gusts. The storms developed near and south of a warm front that extended eastward across the lower Ohio Valley from weak low pressure over southwest Illinois. As surface temperatures cooled with the onset of nocturnal cooling, the storms became mostly elevated in nature. Aloft, a layer of more unstable air persisted due to moist south-southeasterly flow aloft. Most-unstable layer capes in the 1000 to 850 mb layer remained near 1000 j/kg at night. The primary severe weather hazard with these elevated storms was large hail. Effective bulk wind shear values near 30 to 35 knots were marginally favorable for organized convection. The main hazard late in the night and early the following morning was heavy rain. A slow-moving cluster of storms regenerated during the very early morning hours, producing some road flooding in the Hopkinsville area as well as minor flooding of the Little River.
episodes.185068: On the night of September 27th, a warm front stretched east through southern Indiana from a low pressure system that was over southern Illinois. Even though instability was limited from diurnal warming because of cloud cover, enhanced upper forcing caused convection to develop over southern Indiana south of the warm front, and a couple thunderstorms became severe, producing severe winds and dropping large hail in a few isolated areas of north central Kentucky.
episodes.186127: An upper-level low extended a deep trough into the Mid-South. An embedded shortwave combined with enough instability to fire up a few storms across Tennessee.
episodes.186135: Widespread showers and thundestorms developed between a ridge over the western Atlantic and lower pressures over the northwestern Caribbean Sea.  Isolated convective gale-force wind gusts occurred offshore Islamorada.

A house was struck by lightning, starting a damaging fire. While firefighters were battling the fire, another lightning strike occurred about 300 feet away. A firefighter who was next to a fire truck was thrown backward when the lightning struck. The firefighter was shocked and thrown to the ground, causing minor injuries that required treatment at a local hospital.

A water rescue was conducted on Highway 475 after a vehicle became submerged in floodwaters up to the taillights. The Todd County Rescue Squad assisted her out of the vehicle, and she was not injured. The incident occurred closer to the U.S. Highway 68 end of Highway 475.
Minor flooding on the Little River caused some inundation of low-lying fields and cropland. A few streets were flooded in town.
